sentences.text: 1.2 To complete narration of facts, we may add that the marriage between the parties was solemnized on 14.05.2021.
On 26.07.2023, the petitioner filed maintenance petition under section 125 Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
On 28.04.2023, the respondent filed divorce petition.

Transfer of the aforesaid cases have been prayed for in the present petitions.
2.
Vide order dated 29.10.2025 by this Court, the matter was referred for mediation to the Supreme Court Mediation Center.
As per the report received from the mediation center, the dispute has been settled between the parties.
The terms have been reduced into writing vide Settlement Agreement dated 15.01.2026.
The wife stated that she is willing to go for divorce by mutual consent on receiving a sum of  10,00,000/- as alimony for her past, present and future claims.
Another sum of 5,00,000/- have been agreed for the maintenance of the son namely Pranav @ Maruti born from the wedlock.
The said amount was agreed to be paid by the husband when the application under Article 142 of the Constitution of India was to be listed for hearing before this Court.
On payment of the said amount, no further claims were to survive between the parties.
2.1 The issue regarding custody, maintenance and visitation rights for the child is also settled.
The custody of the child is to remain with the mother.
2.2 Along with the Settlement Agreement, list of 13 cases pending between the parties has been attached as Annexure A-1.

The same reads as under:
(i) Petitioner/ Wife also file a case under the Provisions of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 as Criminal Case No.539 of 2023 before the Ld.
Civil Judge (Jr. Div)  FTC, Baghpat, U.P.

(xii) The Respondent/ Husband filed Case No. Complaint Case No.1305 of 2025 Deepak Sharma vs State, P.S. Farsh Bazar pending before the court of Judicial Magistrate First Class Sh. Akhil Malik Shahadra District Karkardooma Court, Delhi.
(xiii) The Petitioners brother Dhruv Dev filed a Criminal Case No. 3977 of 2025 bearing FIR No.324 of 2024 P.S. Farsh Bazar (State vs Deepak Sharma) before the Ld. Akhil Malik JMFC 02 Shahadra KKD, Delhi.
3. It was agreed that in view of the settlement arrived at between the parties, the aforesaid cases should be disposed of as settled.
FIR No.115 of 2023 dated 15.03.2023, FIR No.116 of 2023 dated 15.03.2023 and FIR No.324 of 2024 dated 14.06.2024 may be quashed as compromised.
4. The parties have filed an application under Article 142 of the Constitution of India for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent.
5. Today, the respondent has appeared before the Court along with his counsel whereas the petitioner no.1 has joined through video conferencing.
Both the parties have endorsed the terms of settlement.

The two Demand Drafts bearing No.000810 for  8,70,000/- dated 16.01.2026 and No.000811 for  6,30,000/- dated 16.01.2026, drawn on AU Small Finance Bank respectively, have been handed over by the respondent to the learned counsel for the petitioner for onward transmission to her.

sentences.text: 3 6. Considering the settlement of dispute between the parties, we allow the application filed under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and the marriage of the petitioner-wife/Pragya Vats @ Nancy and the respondent- husband/Deepak Sharma, solemnized on 14.05.2021, stands dissolved by way of decree of divorce by mutual consent.

The parties shall abide by the terms of the Settlement Agreement dated 15.01.2026.
7.
Decree sheet be prepared.
Terms of settlement shall form part of the decree.

8. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties, all the cases mentioned in paragraph No.2.2 filed by the parties against each other shall stand disposed of without any further action by either of them.
The criminal complaints or the FIRs and all proceedings subsequent thereto shall stand quashed as compromised.
9. The Registry shall forward copy of this order to all the Courts concerned for placing the same on respective files and consign them to record.
10. The efforts made by Mr. Abdulrahiman Tamboli, learned Mediator/Advocate to settle the dispute between the parties are appreciated.
11. Accordingly, the present Transfer Petition is disposed of.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

...J. (RAJESH BINDAL) ...J. (VIJAY BISHNOI) New Delhi;
February 04, 2026.
